story.title: China Expels Two Senior Military Leaders Amid Anti-Corruption Drive
story.summary: China has expelled two high-ranking generals from the Communist Party due to allegations of corruption and disloyalty. This action is part of an ongoing anti-corruption campaign within the military. One of the expelled leaders, Zhang Youxia, was the highest-ranked general in the country, serving as a vice chairman on the Central Military Commission.

explore_lenses.label: How did the case move from probe to expulsion?
explore_lenses.title: An eight-month progression through party and state bodies
explore_lenses.summary: The September expulsions culminate a process that began with announced investigations in January and formal removal from the state Central Military Commission in August. The case is part of a longer military-focused disciplinary campaign under Xi Jinping.

claims.text: China's Defense Ministry announced on January 24, 2026 that Zhang, then a Central Military Commission vice chairman, and Liu, then chief of the Joint Staff Department, were under investigation for suspected serious disciplinary and legal violations.
China's National People's Congress Standing Committee formally removed both men from the state Central Military Commission in late August, before the September 21 party and military expulsions.

The Chinese leadership presents the action as evidence that its military anti-corruption effort has "zero tolerance" and applies regardless of rank; this is the party-state's stated rationale for the campaign.

The Chinese leadership presents the action as evidence that its military anti-corruption effort has "zero tolerance" and applies regardless of rank; this is the party-state's stated rationale for the campaign.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Public reporting and official statements do not independently establish which alleged conduct prompted the January investigations or when it occurred.

explore_lenses.label: What changes at the top of China's military?
explore_lenses.title: Two former holders of pivotal command posts are out
explore_lenses.summary: Zhang had been the top uniformed officer as senior Central Military Commission vice chairman, while Liu led the Joint Staff Department. Their removal creates vacancies in China’s highest military leadership, but no replacements were announced in the expulsion notice.

claims.text: Before their removal, Zhang was the senior vice chairman of the Central Military Commission and China's highest-ranking uniformed officer; Liu was a commission member and chief of its Joint Staff Department.
The September 21 official statement confirms their expulsion from both the Communist Party and military service, but does not name successors for their former command roles.

Chinese military media argued in January that disciplining the two would strengthen party control, political cohesion, and military combat effectiveness; that is an official assessment rather than an independently verifiable operational outcome.

story_report.summary: China expelled senior generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the Communist Party and military service on September 21 after allegations of corruption and disloyalty. Zhang, formerly the senior vice chairman of the Central Military Commission and China’s highest-ranking uniformed officer, and Liu, the Joint Staff Department chief, had already been removed from the state military commission. The expulsions remove two leading officers from their posts, though no successors were named publicly.

sections.heading: Investigations preceded the expulsions
sections.body: China’s Defense Ministry said on January 24 that Zhang and Liu were under investigation for suspected serious disciplinary and legal violations. In late August, the National People’s Congress Standing Committee formally removed both from the state Central Military Commission, preceding the September 21 party and military expulsions. Public disclosures have not independently specified the alleged conduct behind the investigations or when it occurred.

sections.heading: Party frames action as zero tolerance
sections.body: Chinese authorities presented the action as part of a military anti-corruption drive that applies regardless of rank. State and military media said disciplining the two officers would reinforce party control, political cohesion and combat effectiveness. Those claimed institutional effects are the official assessment, not independently verified operational outcomes.

unresolved.text: No confirmed public account has identified replacements for Zhang or Liu, changes to the military chain of command, or measurable effects on People’s Liberation Army readiness.

related_stories.title: Ukraine Launches Massive Drone Attack on Moscow, Causing Casualties and Damage
related_stories.summary: Ukraine has launched a significant drone attack involving over 1,000 drones targeting Russia, marking the largest assault on Moscow to date. The attack coincided with the final day of tightly controlled parliamentary elections in Russia. Reports indicate that the assault resulted in damage to an oil refinery and a residential building, with at least two fatalities confirmed in Moscow. The mayor of Moscow described the event as the largest drone attack on the city.

related_stories.summary: Israeli attacks in Gaza have reportedly killed four Palestinians, including a child and a woman, according to health officials. The strikes occurred despite a ceasefire agreement signed in October. Several others were also injured during the incidents across the territory.

related_stories.title: Patrick Clancy Discusses Forgiveness and Grief After Mistrial
related_stories.summary: In his first interview since the mistrial of his ex-wife, Patrick Clancy spoke about the tragic loss of their three children. He expressed that he forgave her to avoid being consumed by anger and grief. Clancy shared details about the events leading up to the deaths of his children and how he has been coping with the aftermath.

related_stories.title: Three Arrested in Connection with Series of Killings of Women in South Africa
related_stories.summary: Two women and a man have been arrested in connection with one of several recent killings of women in South Africa, which has raised significant concern over violence against women in the country. The arrests occurred on the outskirts of Johannesburg, where multiple incidents have been reported in recent months.
